sections.preamble: You answer questions about a single medical image. Follow the answer format requested in the user message exactly.

content.text:
This is one axial slice of a T2-weighted fat-suppressed MRI (radiological convention: patient right on image left, anterior at top). It contains a soft-tissue mass.

The left panel is the clean image; the right panel shows numbered marks. Choose the ONE mark that lies inside the tumor, as close to its centre as possible. End your reply with a final line exactly: ANSWER: <mark number>

The slice shows the chest wall, with a heterogeneous bright mass in the anterior soft tissue (roughly x 300–440, y 110–210 in the left panel). On the right panel this corresponds to x of about 1085–1225.

Marks in or near that region:
- 390 at (1118, 124): near the upper-left edge of the mass.
- 389 at (1149, 131): inside the bright area.
- 370 at (1205, 112): at the upper edge.
- 400 at (1205, 174): inside the bright area, toward the right side.
- 380 at (1168, 211): at the lower edge.
- 388 at (1081, 174): outside the left edge, over the muscle.

The bright mass centre is around (1150, 150) in the right panel, i.e. about (370, 150) in the left panel. Mark 389 is the closest to that centre, and it sits within the bright heterogeneous tissue.

ANSWER: 389
